questions.q: What two sections does a newly created lakehouse start with?
options: Bronze and Gold, matching medallion architecture exactly
A single unified storage area with no distinction
Files (unstructured storage) and Tables (real, queryable Delta tables)
Notebooks and Pipelines
questions.explain: Both are already backed by OneLake and ready for content, with no separate storage step required.

questions.q: How does the Files section relate to Databricks & Delta Lake's bronze layer concept?
options: It makes the bronze instinct literal — landing raw data exactly as it arrived, before deciding anything about its shape
Files is only used for storing notebooks, not raw data
Files always requires a schema to be defined before any upload
Files has no relationship to bronze; it's purely for temporary scratch work
questions.explain: This is Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 26's bronze layer instinct, made literal in Fabric's UI.

questions.q: What happens when you use "Load to Tables" on a CSV file?
options: The CSV file itself is converted in place into a Delta table
No schema inference happens; every column becomes a string
Fabric reads the source file, infers a schema, and writes it out as a new, separate Delta table — the original CSV in Files is untouched
The CSV file is deleted after loading
questions.explain: This is the exact inferSchema cost from Foundations Lesson 40, now happening behind a UI click.

questions.q: Why doesn't loading a CSV into Tables modify the original file in Files?
options: The original file is automatically deleted once loaded
Files and Tables share the exact same underlying storage location, so both are affected
It does modify the original file, converting it to Delta format in place
Load to Tables creates a new, separate Delta table built from the file — the original file itself is never altered
questions.explain: This is a real, structural distinction — Files and Tables are genuinely separate areas within the lakehouse.

questions.q: What format does the Tables section use underneath, and why does that matter?
options: JSON documents with no transactional guarantees at all
A completely proprietary Fabric-only format unrelated to Delta Lake
Real Delta tables — the same format from Databricks & Delta Lake's entire Chapter 2, with the same transaction log and ACID guarantees
Plain CSV files renamed with a .table extension
questions.explain: This is why the previous course's Delta Lake material transfers directly into Fabric's Tables section.
